title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Timber floor restoration
audience: Any home-service operator, including solo operators, starting or growing a business.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: "I will sand your floors" is a service. "I will sand and finish the 20 square metre lounge room to the finish agreed on the scope sheet, leave it ready to walk on within the agreed days, and redo any patch that does not match the agreed sheen at no charge" is an offer. The customer buys a floor they can use, and the certainty that the agreed finish will be delivered.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: Set a clear outcome, such as a refinished room with a named finish; a time frame, such as the days the room is out of use; the work the customer must do, such as moving furniture and keeping pets out; the certainty you give, such as a written scope sheet and photos; and the risk you carry. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Separate refinish, buff and add-ons on the offer
instruction.body: A refinish and a buff-and-polish are different jobs with different prices, so show them as separate lines. The Oneflare cost guide gives a general refinish range of $25 to $50 per square metre, a buffing figure of around $25 per square metre (rising to $30 for older or historic homes), and a sander hire add-on that it says can add $8 to $12 to the cost of polishing, with the unit not stated (Oneflare, no date shown). The same guide's state table is unverified, because its unit is unclear, so do not use it as your rate. Show each line with its unit, and say whether it is per square metre or per hour.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction and setting certainty
instruction.body: Make the booking, the moving of furniture and the handover easy. Agree in writing how long the room stays out of use, who moves the furniture and what the customer must keep off the floor. Give the customer a scope sheet that lists the sanding grit stages, the number of coats and the sheen, so the finish can be checked against what was agreed. Photos of the floor are useful, but photos that show people need the privacy steps in the safety section.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: The Australian Consumer Law consumer guarantees apply to services. They require due care and skill, delivery within a reasonable time where none is agreed, and fitness for any stated purpose, and a business cannot remove them by contract or notice (ACCC, last modified 17 July 2026). A finish warranty that you choose to add is an extra promise on top of those guarantees (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). The research found no verified floor-finish manufacturer warranty, so check your product supplier's terms before you promise one. Do not state a result, such as a hardness or sheen level, that you cannot show.

instruction.heading: Price the offer as one total
instruction.body: Show one total for each room and one total for the job, and say whether GST is included. The ACCC's price display guidance (2 October 2026) says a total must include unavoidable fees. Price each room from its area and cost, then check it against your cost and time before you decide on any premium.

procedure: Write the finish outcome for each room in one sentence a customer would repeat.
Set a time frame for each room that you have checked against your own completed jobs, and record how often you meet it.
List what the customer must do, such as moving furniture and keeping pets out, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a scope sheet with grit stages, coats and sheen, and sign-off.
Decide the guarantee and check that you can afford it.
Price each room from its measured area, show refinish and buff as separate lines, and check the rate against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A 20 square metre hardwood room needs a refinish. The Oneflare guide gives a general refinish range of $25 to $50 per square metre, with the location not given and no date shown.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the quote show the room, and what does the sourced range tell the owner?
workedExamples.reasoning: The quote shows the area, the rate per square metre and the total, so the customer sees the unit. The sourced range gives two checks: 20 square metres at $25 is $500, and at $50 is $1,000. The owner sets the rate from their own cost and time, then confirms that it sits within the range or explains why it does not. The range is a sense check. It is not a price the owner must quote, and the location and date of the source must be noted.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative: the same 20 square metre room is a polish-only job with a buff at around $25 per square metre, and the sander hire add-on at $8 to $12 per square metre. The source does not state the unit for the add-on.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the polish-only job cost on the quote, and what must be confirmed first?
workedExamples.reasoning: If the buff is $25 per square metre alone, 20 square metres is $500. If the sander hire add-on is also per square metre, the figure becomes $660 at $8 and $740 at $12. Because the unit of the add-on is not stated, the owner confirms with the hire supplier that the add-on is per square metre before it is quoted that way. Otherwise the add-on is shown as a fixed line.

equipmentAndPpe: Scope sheet with grit stages, number of coats, sheen and exclusions
Room measurement sheet with area and per-square-metre rate
Written workmanship warranty template, kept separate from the consumer guarantees
Respiratory protection and dust controls as set out in the safety section, and the safety data sheet for each finish

commonErrors.error: Quoting per hour from a per-square-metre table, or the reverse.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the unit beside every rate, and confirm it before the quote is sent.

commonErrors.error: Treating the state table in the Oneflare guide as a reliable rate. Gap: the table's unit is unclear and it is unverified.
commonErrors.prevention: Use your own cost and time, and use the general range only as a sense check, with its source and date recorded.

commonErrors.error: Promising a finish result or sheen you cannot show.
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the finish on the scope sheet in terms you can demonstrate, and state any warranty as an extra promise in writing.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer guarantees for services apply under the Australian Consumer Law, and a business cannot exclude them by contract (ACCC, 17 July 2026). Business guidance only: this lesson does not grant any licence or authority.

Victoria only: WorkSafe Victoria (reviewed 17 April 2026) says wood dust is classed as carcinogenic to humans, that sanding raises dust levels, and that dust-generating work needs local exhaust ventilation. It also says compressed air should not be used to clear dust, and that a half-face P2 respirator would be sufficient in usual cases. Check the rule for your own state and the work you do.

NSW only: NSW LeadSmart (modified 20 July 2026) says lead paint was used in most homes built in Australia before 1970, and that painted timber floor edges and skirting can contain it. It recommends a professional trained in lead paint work, and says wet sanding and wet scraping are the safest methods. Open-flame torches should not be used. Check the lead rules that apply where you work before sanding painted edges.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A timber floor offer promises a finished room, a scope sheet and a time frame, not an area rate alone.
Show refinish, buff and add-ons as separate lines, each with its unit.
Gap: the research has no dated state-by-state rate, no verified trade body and no property-manager or trade referral channel for timber floors.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a timber floor offer does the customer buy?
options: A finished room with a scope sheet, a time frame and certainty

knowledgeChecks.question: What unit does the Oneflare general refinish range use?
options: Per hour, for the whole crew
Per room, regardless of its size

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the state table in the Oneflare guide not be used as your rate?
options: Its unit is unclear and the table is unverified
It is the official ACCC rate for every state
It has been checked against every state's rules
It includes the price of the owner's vehicle

officialReferences.title: What the ACCC does: consumer rights and guarantees (ACCC)
